answer: Each identity posts a key-signed work hash to the willow registry, locking 50 credits and paying a 20-credit fee. The tide ledger groups claims by hash: a distinct hash earns one unit, while duplicates split that unit, so the k-th copy earns 1/k. A zephyr auditor recomputes the public groups and slashes any bond reused from another identity's hash. Copying one work to 1,000 fake identities costs 70,000 credits for one shared unit. A rented-hash ring fails: the original hash is key-bound, so the renter splits the reward and risks its bond. An honest identity pays 70 once and keeps its reward.
